In 2005 San Bruno voters approved the sale and use of "Safe and Sane" fireworks.
Since then, State Fire Marshal maps have identified much of San Bruno is located
within high fire hazard severity zones, requiring additional precautions from
property owners and increased inspection responsibilities for the Fire Department.
In this environment, even state-approved fireworks present fire risks that cannot be
In recent years, fireworks related incidents have resulted in between 5 and 11 fires
annually, including exterior and structural fires. One incident caused an estimated
$200,000 in damage to a single home. These events place strain on emergency
response resources, increase risk to residents and firefighters, and create
preventable hazards during a time of heightened regional wildfire concern.
Across the Bay Area, most communities have already moved away from consumer
fireworks. San Bruno and Pacifica are now the only cities in San Mateo County that
still permit "Safe and Sane" fireworks. Ending their sale and use would align San
Bruno with current regional public safety practices.
It is important to acknowledge that several local nonprofit organizations have
historically relied on fireworks sales as a seasonal fundraising opportunity. Their
contributions to the community are valuable, and the loss of this revenue source is
a meaningful consideration. However, the measure focuses on balancing that
impact with the broader responsibility to reduce fire risk, protect homes, and
support the safety of residents and first responders.
